correctness.rationale: Normalize x=BF/C and u=BHM: q=(A/C)*x/[(1+x)((D+u)x+u)]. Differentiating gives sign u-(D+u)x², maximizer x=√(u/(D+u)) for M>0, continuous envelope limit at M=0. Thus F’/F<=Q(M_s(t))-delta_F and integration yields the exact comparison bound for each F(0)>0. Strict eventual negative limsup average gives global exponential decay; for periodic profiles the time average is a single period integral. Independent 80-digit quadrature with the same source-derived K=416990000/20553, A=2499/40000, C=2/25, D=51/200, H=1/10, delta_F=1/25 gives 0.038221770950267804205... at s=120000 (<.04), and 0.073750171814416675109... at s=60000 (>.04). The result says nothing about persistence when the sufficient test fails. The application is separated from proof: quadrature establishes numerical strict inequality, analytic envelope establishes global theorem.

value.rationale: A natural gap is that pointwise release thresholds do not explain why periodically subthreshold release eliminates the mosquito population in the motivating simulations. The explicit integral envelope closes that source-specific question and supplies a checkable sufficient criterion for arbitrary nonnegative periodic input, relevant for periodic-control design, while carefully not claiming necessity.

final_claim: For the specified stage-sex sterile-mosquito scalar nonautonomous equation, the exact per-capita upper envelope Q(M)=A/[C(√(D+BHM)+√(BHM))²] yields a sufficient extinction test limsup_T average Q(M_s)<delta_F, applying analytically to the 120000-scale sinusoid from He–Li–Liu that violates the prior pointwise lower threshold.
